# Kiama Art Gallery

> > A comprehensive exploration of 19th and early 20th century European art movements, with particular focus on French Impressionism, Romanticism, Symbolism, and the artists who shaped modern art.

Kiama Art Gallery's blog chronicles art historian Andrea Hope's personal journey through major art movements, featuring detailed analyses of masterworks, artist biographies, and travel accounts from European museums. The site emphasizes the evolution of modern art from Romanticism through Impressionism to Expressionism, with special attention to women artists and the cultural contexts that shaped artistic innovation.

## Key Topics

- Impressionism
- French Art & Paris Salon
- 19th Century Art History
- Romanticism & Symbolism
- Women Artists
- Claude Monet, Camille Pissarro, Alfred Sisley
- Édouard Manet, Edgar Degas, Pierre-Auguste Renoir
- Paul Gauguin, Gustave Courbet
- Plein-Air Painting
- Expressionism
- Political & Social Commentary in Art
- European Museum Collections
- Artist Biographies
- École des Beaux-Arts

## Impressionism & the Paris Salon

- [The Impressionist Exhibitions](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/03/20/the-impressionist-exhibitions): Eight Impressionist exhibitions in Paris from 1874 to 1886
- [Impressionism – Camille Pissarro](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/05/24/impressionism-camille-pissarro): Camille Pissarro's central role in all eight Impressionist exhibitions
- [Impressionism – Alfred Sisley, Landscapes](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/05/31/impressionism-alfred-sisley-landscapes): Alfred Sisley's dedication to Impressionist landscape painting techniques
- [Impressionism – Eva Gonzalés](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/07/23/impressionism-eva-gonzales): Eva Gonzalés as Manet's only formal pupil and Impressionist artist

## Romanticism & Realism

- [Romanticism – Géricault, Raft of the Medusa, 1818-19](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/04/16/romanticism-gericault-raft-of-the-medusa-1818-19): Géricault's masterpiece depicting human suffering after the Méduse shipwreck
- [Romanticism – Eugène Delacroix, Liberty Leading the People, 1830](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/04/20/romanticism-eugene-delacroix-liberty-leading-the-people-1830): Delacroix's iconic Romantic painting of the 1830 Trois Glorieuses uprising
- [Realism – Gustave Courbet, The Stonebreakers, 1849](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/04/23/realism-gustave-courbet-the-stonebreakers-1849): Courbet's realistic depiction of working-class suffering and deprivation

## Symbolism & Expressionism

- [Symbolism – A short introduction](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2016/05/13/symbolism): Introduction to Symbolist movement in late 19th century art and literature
- [Symbolism – Edvard Munch](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2016/09/22/symbolism-edvard-munch): Edvard Munch's Symbolist works including The Scream and The Sick Child
- [Käthe Kollwitz – Expressionist Printer and Sculptor](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2018/01/16/kathe-kollwitz-expressionist-printer-and-sculpture): Käthe Kollwitz's political graphic art and role in Women's Art Association

## Modern Art & Special Topics

- [Modern Art Appreciation – Influences on artists' styles](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/03/02/modern-art-appreciation-influences-on-artists-styles): Explores how artists respond to cultural norms and balance creativity with commerce
- [Representations of Venus – 1480 to 1980](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2017/05/09/representations-of-venus-1480-to-1980): 500 years of Venus mythology from Botticelli to modern interpretations
- [Henri Rousseau – Tigers and Imagination](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2017/01/04/henri-rousseau-tigers-and-imagination): Henri Rousseau's jungle paintings combining imagination and exotic imagery
- [Raoul Dufy and the Colour Blue](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2019/10/09/raoul-dufy-and-the-colour-blue): Raoul Dufy's distinctive use of blue at Museum of Modern Art, Le Havre

## Women Artists

- [Salons des Femmes](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/03/26/salons-des-femmes): Union of Women Painters and Sculptors founded by Hélène Bertaux in 1881
- [Impressionism – Eva Gonzalés](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2015/07/23/impressionism-eva-gonzales): Eva Gonzalés as Manet's only formal pupil and Impressionist artist
- [Käthe Kollwitz – Expressionist Printer and Sculptor](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2018/01/16/kathe-kollwitz-expressionist-printer-and-sculpture): Käthe Kollwitz's political graphic art and role in Women's Art Association

## European Museum Visits & Travel

- [Picasso Museum – Antibes](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2018/07/16/picasso-museum-antibes): Andrea Hope's visit to Musée Picasso Antibes during European holiday
- [Red, White and Blue, and Yellow](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2018/07/18/red-white-and-blue-and-yellow): Van Gogh's Yellow House pilgrimage in Arles, Provence during 2018 travels
- [Surprised at the Leopold](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2018/08/03/surprised-at-the-leopold): Gustav Klimt's early works at Leopold Museum, Vienna during 2018 travels
- [The Heidi Horten Collection at the Leopold Museum in Vienna](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2018/08/07/the-heidi-horten-collection-at-the-leopold-museum): 170+ works from Expressionism to Pop Art in Heidi Horten Collection, Vienna

## Optional

- [Learning to Appreciate Art – My Accidental Journey](https://kiamaartgallery.wordpress.com/2017/12/04/learning-to-appreciate-art-my-accidental-journey): Personal journey from rural NSW to art appreciation through photography
